subject.summary: One run of NetLogo's Fireflies. The run's pulse rising with time: one ring per tick, its area the share of turtles in that state then (it was shown (hidden? turned false)), so turtles on their own make a thin, ragged column and turtles in step make wide plates with nothing between.

sources.title: A construct of a NetLogo run
A run of Fireflies (NetLogo 7.0.4), recorded with construct.nls

facts.value: Y is up. The floor is the NetLogo world, 10 m across its longer side; height is time, 10 m from tick 0 to tick 670.
it was shown (hidden? turned false), 60.5 times per turtle on average
at most 100% of the turtles at once; the most at once early in the run 15%, late 100%
half at once: 66% of the turtles at tick 325
all at once: 100% of the turtles at tick 466

facts.note: Where the synchrony formed: 0.24 at the start, 1.00 by tick 670, and it stays near there for the rest of the run. The whole run is in the recording (and in the film); --window whole draws all of it.
The data as the bridge drew it from the recording: 6 parts (world, time-axis, pulse-*, pulse-all, landmark-* (2)), the run's facts and the view. The audit refuses the scene if any of it changes.

how: Height is time, from tick 0 on the floor to tick 670 at the top: one ring for each tick.
This shows ticks 0 to 670, where the synchrony formed (0.24 at the start, 1.00 by tick 670); after that it stays near there. The whole run is in the recording and its film.
A ring's area is the share of turtles in that state at that tick (it was shown (hidden? turned false)); the faint circle at the floor and the top is every turtle at once.
A thin, ragged column is turtles on their own rhythms; wide plates with nothing between are turtles in step, all at once.
Where the column opens into plates is where they fell into step.
